question: Why does a golden dataset need to stay fixed rather than being regenerated each time a system is evaluated?
answer: A golden dataset needs to stay fixed rather than being regenerated each time a system is evaluated because if the test set drifts every time you evaluate, you cannot tell whether a score change reflects a real improvement or just a different, easier set of questions. [chunk-id::0] Additionally, treating this as an actual template with named, testable slots makes prompt changes reviewable and their effects measurable against a golden dataset. Keeping the dataset fixed allows for consistent evaluation across different system configurations and changes. [chunk-id::1]
